Night-flying mosquitoes that were beleived to be ranging flight would alter their heading to fly towards inanimate physical objects. Mosquitos is proved that reponse to the length of colour in simple shaped objects.

The insect rests during walking on a supporting triangle, formed by the anterior and posterior limb on one side and the middle limb on the other, while it carries forward the other three legs.

The fore leg acts as a tractor; the middle leg serves for support, lifting the body on its own side and together with the hind leg raising the posterior part of the body; the hind leg acts as a propulsor and also turns the body in the horizontal plane. The three legs forming the tripod for a time being are not lifted simultaneously but in the order: i)fore-leg ii)opposite middle leg iii)hind-leg.

Some larvae walk by means of their thoracic legs in the same manner as adult forms; but they are often aided by provisional modifications of the abdomen.

Larvae use their abdominal muscles to cause a lateral flexure of the abdomen. The massive abdominal muscles that provide the power for larval locomotion persist through the pupal and pharate-adult stages.
The movement of adult mosquitoes in the air currents. Defined as slowly falling at less than 45 degrees from the horizontal.

The lower Diptera (Tipulids) have long thin abdomens and long legs which probably ensure their stabilityduring flight. In higher forms (Muscids) their wings-beats create a resultant force which is equal to or greater than the weight of the insect.
The period between stimulus and contraction.

The precise modulations of contractions of the individual muscles. When expressed together or in a specific sequence, these contractions embody the displacements in space that are interpreted as the expression of particular behaviors.
The part of the peripheral nervous system that acts as a control system, maintaining homeostasis in the body.
Arises during embryonic development by an ingrowth from the dorsal wall of the stomodaeum which later requires connexion with the brain.

Innervates the sexual organs and the posterior segments of the gut is composed of nerves arising from the composite terminal ganglion of the abdomen. The mid-gut, the heart and the Malpighian tubes show continued movements after separation from the central nervous system. The control of these movements is attributed to peripheral ganglion cells; and it has been suggested that it is this autonomous peripheral system that should be called the sympathetic nervous system.
The endocrine system is an integrated system of small organs that involve the release of extracellular signaling molecules known as hormones.
A nematode living in slow-moving freshwater, whose larval stages parasitize mosquito larvae.

A fish is any aquatic vertebrate animal that is typically ectothermic (or cold-blooded), covered with scales, and equipped with two sets of paired fins and several unpaired fins. Fish are abundant in the sea and in fresh water, with species being known from mountain streams (e.g. char and gudgeon) as well as in the deepest depths of the ocean (e.g., gulpers and anglerfish).

The mosquitofish (Gambusia affinis) is a species of freshwater fish, also commonly known simply by its generic name, gambusia, although such usage is ambiguous. It is sometimes called the western mosquitofish, to distinguish it from the eastern mosquitofish (G. holbrooki). It is a member of the family Poeciliidae of order Cyprinodontiformes. The genus name 'gambusia' is derived from the Cuban Spanish term 'gambusino', meaning useless.
Any organsim that parasitizes mosquitoes.
A fish that feeds on mosquito larvae.
Annual fishes are species that belong to the family Cyprinodontidae and which complete their life cycles within a year, their eggs requiring a dry period to develop fully.
An larvivorous annual fish.
An larvivorous annual fish.

The events occurring 2 to 3 days before the first malarial paroxysm during which the patient experiences mild symptoms that include malaise, fatigue, lassitude, a desire to stretch the limbs, headache, dizziness, pain in different areas of the body, anorexia, nausea and slight fever.
A general therapeutic procedure applied for malaria.
The use of defined chemical agents to treat or control disease.

A role borne by an antiparasitic chemical compound  in virtue of the fact that is has antiparasitic disposition and it is applied to an anatomical entity of a living organism to provide prophylaxis from malaria.
A parasite causing malaria.
An inherited condition that results in a deficiency in glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase.
Ovalocytosis is an inherited condition in which a person's red blood cells, which are supposed to be round, instead have a slightly oval or elliptical shape.
A coma persisting for at least 30 minutes after a convulsion.
The fact that an endophilic species rests inside the house after the meal.
The fact that an exophilic species will never go indoors.
The fact that an endophilic species will go outdoors for resting after the meal.
The ability of a vector to acquire a pathogen and to successfully transmit it to another susceptible host.
Protein molecules are cleaved into large peptides by proteinases (also called endopeptidases).
The hydrolysis of peptide bonds by a class of peptidases which are characterised by the presence of a serine residue in the active center of the enzyme.
The cleavage of the lipids that are contained in mosquitoes' meal by enzymes, such as carboxylesterases, acetylesterases, arylesterases, that are present in the midgut of adult female mosquitoes.
The cleavage of glycosidic linkages by specific enzymes, carbohydrases.
The large peptides are progressively shortened by peptidases (more specifically called exopeptidases).

The sequence of events that begins with the response of one individual to another of opposite sex and ends with insemination and parting. Mating often is proceded by swarming or other forms of epigamic behaviour.
The nervous arcs through which co-ordination is effected lie in the thoracic ganglia.
Two modes of feeding have been distinguished in male mosquitoes and one additional mode in females: water ingestion, nectar feeding and, for females only, blood feeding.
A small volume of water is imbibed and passed into the midgut.
The first phase of the blood feeding; from time of alighting on the host to the time the stylets start to penetrate the skin.
The phase of the blood feeding from first penetration of the skin to the first appearance of blood in the fascicle and cessation of palpal vibrations.
The phase of the blood feeding from first appearance of blood in the fascicle to the start of withdrawal.
The phase of the blood feeding from first straightening of the forelegs to complete removal of the stylets from the skin.
A meal acquired from two or more hosts, which may have been of the same species (single-species mixed meal) or different species (multi-species mixed meal).
A blood meal resulting from a single feed. It may be complete or, as a result of interruption, incomplete.
A second, third or yet further blood meal acquired in a single gonotrophic cycle through supplementary feeding.
During a single gonotrophic cycle, the female takes more than one blood meal. Multiple feeding involves multiple host contacts.
Acquisition of a blood meal in two or more parts, the mosquito having left its host while only partly fed, due to disturbance, and having resumed feeding soon afterwards on the same or another host.

Acquisition of additional blood meals after the first during a single gonotrophic cycle, independently of interruption due to disturbance, the feedings being separated by intervals of several hours to a day or more.

concept_name: regulation of food intake in adults
definition: The control of feeding and distribution of food within the gut by integrated responses of the peripheral sensilla, central nervous system and, probably, the stomatogastric system. Feeding generally terminates in response to mechanical stimulation caused by swelling of the gut.
name_normalized: regulation of food intake in adults

definition: The regulation of the sugar intake in mosquitoes using chemosensilla and sugar receptors.
When mosquitoes drink, two control processes are involved: one regulates the destination of the fluid the other regulates the volume that is imbibed.

Female mosquitoes gorge on blood when it is applied by capillary tube to the unsheathed fascicle or offered through an artificial membrane. Whether stimulation of just the larbal sensilla with blood is sufficient to induce drinking is not known, but certainly stimulation of both larbal and cibarial sensilla is sufficient.

The sequence of behaviour patterns exhibited by mosquitoes responding to hosts over a distance. Host-seeking behaviour terminates once feeding is initiated and blood ingestion begins. For each species, host-finding activity is exhibited during one or more periods in the diel.
Activation is the first response to host cues; it is the initial response in a sequence of behaviours that ends with arrival at the host.
The navigation of the mosquitoes towards potential hosts through their responses to a variety of cues emanating from them. Some host cues are chemical and others are physical.
The resting of females in their host's proximity after they had approached them and before making a final approach and feeding.
The final stage of host finding; it comprises four steps.
The first step of short-range approach, alighting and exploration; from the perception of cues by the mosquito to the approach of the host.

concept_name: descent to the body surface and alighting
definition: The second step of the short-range approach, alighting and exploration.
name_normalized: descent to the body surface and alighting

concept_name: exploration and examination of the body surface
definition: In this step the mosquito walks over the body, rapidly tapping the surface with its labella, and it may fly from one body region to another in order to find a region of vascularized skin into which it can drive its stylets.
name_normalized: exploration and examination of the body surface

definition: The digestion of blood and nectar. The midgut is the principal organ of digestion, but dissaccharides ingested in nectar are at least partly hydrolysed in the crop by a salivary enzyme.
The regulation of enzyme synthesis by the presence of blood in the midgut or not.

concept_name: absorption of the products of digestion
definition: For the female: digestion of blood proteins yields amino acids which are reconstituted in the mosquito's fat body as proteinaceous yolk. This is important for oogenesis. For both sexes: Plant juices provide an important energy source. They are the only food sources for males.
name_normalized: absorption of the products of digestion

definition: The formation of a membrane which is deposited around the ingested blood mass.
The formation of vitellogenin in the fat body. It is synthesized first as precursors which undergo proteolytic cleavage into two or more subunits.
The act of sexual intercourse, during which the genitalia are engaged and the aedeagus inserted, and semen is passed to the female. It usually lasts a few seconds.
Developing oocytes accumulate proteinaceous yolk by internalizing large amounts of circulating vitellogenin.
The process occurring when a male first responds to a female, seizing her and establishing genital contact.
The rapid production of urine containing principally water and salts.
The release of the unmodified secretion of the Malpighiann tubules.
The tubular fluid is expelled as urine. Tubular fluids are the unmodified secretion of the Malpighian tubules.
The tubular fluid enters the pylorus from where some may be move forwards for resorption in the midgut.
The portion of the tubular fluid that is not absorbed in the hindgut and is moved posteriorly to the rectum where it is modified producing urine.
During the first day after feeding, deamination of amino acids produces excess nitrogen which is voided in the form of low molecular weight nitrogenous metabolites.
During a single gonotrophic cycle, the female takes only one blood meal.
The fluid intake due to the activity of the cibarial and pharyngeal pumps.
The separation of the labellar lobes following stimulation by sugar of sensilla on the outer surface of the labella.
The searching movements made with the proboscis when the tarsi are stimulated by sugar.
The union of male and female gametes and formation of a zygote in anopheline vectors.
The major pathway by which carbohydrates are degraded in insects for energy release.
The energy contained within fatty acid molecules is made available by b-oxidation of the fatty acid.
The steps of a second, third or yet further meal acquired in a single gonotrophic cycle.
The feeding on sugar.
The process of energy absorption from a physical stimulus by a sensillum and its transmission to sensory neurons.
Behaviour displayed by mosquitoes that feed on a few host species only, while in habitats in which a wide range of potential hosts is present.

In both culicines and anophelines, peritrophic membrane that is secreted in the enterior midgut slowly retracts and twists, forming a plug between the anterior medgut and stomach. A similar plug forms between the stomach and hindgut.
A change in state or activity of a cell or an organism (in terms of movement, secretion, enzyme production, gene expression, etc.) as a result of a toxin stimulus.

concept_name: secretion of peritrophic matrix in adults
synonyms: secretion of peritrophic membrane in adults
definition: All midgut columnal cells secrete the substance of the membrane which is deposited around the ingested blood mass.
name_normalized: secretion of peritrophic matrix in adults

concept_name: secretion of peritrophic matrix in larvae
synonyms: secretion of peritrophic membrane in larvae
definition: The membrane is secreted by a narrow band of cells at the anterior end of the mindgut and is formed as a continuous tube.
name_normalized: secretion of peritrophic matrix in larvae

definition: Is the feeding mode most common used by mosquito larvae.
Immediately after feeding the midgut is hugely distended and for the next hour it is engaged in diuresis.
A few hours after the distention of mindgut a phase of organelle synthesis occurs when additional ribosomes and endoplasmic reticulum are synthesized and organized.
After the organelle synthesis it follows a phase of production of digestive enzymes and absorption of the products of digestion.

The males of a number of diptera taxa aggregate in aerials swarms over conspicuous objects or 'swarm markers'. Conspecific females individually fly to these swarms, but little is known of the responses that take them there. At the assembly stations where male and female insects meet, the females usually are recognized by vision, and among insects that form aerial swarms the eyes of the male are specially developed.

concept_name: formation of assembly near vertebrate host
definition: Males of a number of species of Aedes and Mansonia assemble around the warm-blooded hosts on which the females feed, and attempt to couple with virgin females that also respond to the host.
name_normalized: formation of assembly near vertebrate host

concept_name: formation of assembly at emergence site
definition: In a few species, sexually mature males aggregate at the emergence sites, congregating on or near the water surface. Depending on species, they respond to pupae, to emerging females, to newly emerged females or to teneral females. In most of these species the male antennae are modified. Such males do not respond to the female wing-beat tone. In species in which respond to pupae, the male forelegs are modified. In all of these species, the males beome sexually competent only after inversion of th
name_normalized: formation of assembly at emergence site

definition: The process of gathering at different sites as part of the mating process.

The chemical stimuli are organic and inorganic constituents of host odour. Mosquitos respond to some of these kairomones at a distance from the host as they are carried by the wind, and they respond to some at very short range as they are carried in convection currents.

concept_name: response of flying mosquito to visible object
definition: The insect's natural habitat can evoke a response because of the produced visual images.
name_normalized: response of flying mosquito to visible object

definition: Mosquitoes variably approach or avoid visible objects. The responses of mosquitoes to artificial objects have important implications for trap design, but their biological significance is uncertain.

Mosquitoes (night-flying) may alter their flight paths when confronted with barriers, even when the barriers contain apertures large enough for their passage. Observations showed associations between mosquito flight paths and conspicuous features of the landscape.

Mosquitoes species differ in flight capacity, but to speak of an individual species flight range is incorrect because the distances are greatly affected by weather conditions (i.e. wind) and ecological variables.

Is a persistent and straightened-out movement effected by the animal's own locomotory exertions or by its active embarkation on a vehicle such as wind. Migration depends on some temporary inhibiotion of station-keeping responses, but promotes their eventual disinhibition and recurrence.
Continuous flight.
The steps needed for the intake of nectar and other plant sources.
Feeding on nectar and other plant juices provides an immediate energy source and permits the formation of carbohydrate and lipid reserves.

concept_name: formation of carbohydrate and lipid reserves
definition: Feeding on sugar, and, for females, on blood, leads to accumulations of fat and glycogen.
name_normalized: formation of carbohydrate and lipid reserves

concept_name: release and conservation of energy from sugar
definition: Three major processes are involved in the release of energy from sugars: (i) glycolysis, which ends in the production of pyruvate; (ii) oxidation in the tricarboxylic acid (TCA) cycle; and (iii) further oxidation in the respiratory chain (oxidative phosphorylation).
name_normalized: release and conservation of energy from sugar

concept_name: accumulation and use of the carbohydrate and lipid reserve
definition: The carbohydrate and lipid reserves present in most mosquitoes at emergence are insufficient for more than a few days' life and, for all males and the females of many species, must be replenished by feeding on plant sugars. A portion of the digestion products from blood meals in converted to glycogen and lipids, the proportion varying with species and with size of female.
name_normalized: accumulation and use of the carbohydrate and lipid reserve

As the oocytes move backwards they become surrounded by the follicle cells of somatic origin, which compose the hind part of the germarium, and each oocyte in its follicle forms an egg chamber of the vitellarium. As the oocyte grows the cells finally arrange themselves in a single layer.

During mosquito embryogenesis pole cells form after cleavage energids have entered the posterior periplasm with its polar granules. The pole mirgrate in to two groups and settled in the 6th abdominal segment, where they become surrounded by mesodermal sheaths and form the gonad rudiments. The pole cells are now called primordial germ cells. By the 4th larval instar the ovaries are already distinct and contain cell clusters within a matrix of smaller cells, the interstitial tissue. Gravid females of Culex quinquefasciatus and Cx tarsalis oviposit preferentially on water where already egg rafts have been laid.

The period during which follicles separate from the germania, cell types become visibly distinct , the oocytes become competent to incorporate vitellogenin, and a little growth occurs prior to entry into a resting stage.
The few hours immediately after a blood meal when follicle growth recommences, with the formation of additional microvilli and coated pits, and vitellogenin synthesis starts.

The main period of vitellogenin synthesis and incorporation with rapid oocyte growth, ending with the cessation of vitellogenin synthesis and formation of an intact endochorionic layer between oocyte and epithelial cells.
When the oocyte assumes its mature form and becomes surrounded by an unhardened chorion.

concept_name: rRNA synthesis in oocyte and nurse cells
definition: Histochemical studies combined with the use of radioactive tracers and electron microscopy have largely confirmed that there is active synthesis and emission of RNA from the nucleus, and thence from the nucleus of the oocyte to the cytoplasm. Some of the proteins of the egg are synthetized in the nurse cells and follicular cells.
name_normalized: rrna synthesis in oocyte and nurse cells

definition: The process of the four developmental phases, from the primary follicles to the mature form of the oocyte.
The chorion is the part of the egg shell that is secreted before oviposition by the follicular epithelium, a maternal tissue.

The sense by which the qualities of an object (as color, luminosity, shape, and size) constituting its appearance are perceived through a process in which light rays entering the eye are transformed by the retina into electrical signals that are transmitted to the brain via the optic nerve.
Behaviour displayed by mosquitoes that feed on wider range of hosts, while in habitats in which a wide range of potential hosts is present.

The waves of air pressure which we recognize as sounds may be perceived by insects by two quite different mechanism. The antennae of mosquitoes are mechanosensory transducers which in flight respond to drag forces and to gravitational forces, and in which the males at least are also sensitive to sound waves. Organs of hearing convert the energy of sound waves into electrical signals, and in this way resemble microphones.

The perception of the qualities of sweet, sour, salt and bitter. Gustatory sensilla are uniporous hair or peg sensilla that respond to stimulating molecules in the liquid phase. In mosquitoes they are present on the legs and mouthparts, and the input from the various sensilla is intergrated centrally.

The sense of smell in insects is located chiefly in the antennae. The olfactory sensilla of mosquitoes compromise multiporous hair and peg sensilla on the antennal flagella and multiporous peg sensilla on the maxillary palps.
The process of any action or reaction of a vector organism in response to external or internal stimuli.

It is found that the behavioural activities of adult mosquitoes take place at particular times of day and night, which vary between species and the timing is controlled by endogeous or so-called circadian rythms, which are reset daily by the change from light to dark at sunset.
The analysis of the movements of the mosquito's larva into a series of reflexes or observed correlations between stimulus and response.
The analysis of the movements of the mosquito's pupa into a series of reflexes or observed correlations between stimulus and response.
Any behavioral process during the adult stage of a vector organism.

The circulation of the blood is maintained by a system of muscular pumps and fibro-muscular septa. The haemolymph has many functions. It provides the tissues that it bathes with nutrients and metabolic intermediates, and it provides a medium for the transport of their chemical wastes.
Oragnic material of almost every kind in nature serve as food for insects. The process of nutrition starts with the ingestion of food and ends with the digestion.
The process of taking a substance into the body through the mouth.
The process with which oxygen is conveyed from the atmosphere to the tissues, and how the carbon dioxide resulting from oxidation in the tissues is eliminated.
The intake of oxygen in the adult mosquito.

Larvae use an open respiratory system which impose limitations to the requirement for access to atmospheric oxygen. The mosquito larval tracheal system consist of two wide dorsal longitydinal trunks, two narrower lateral, and branches which run from them to all regions of the body.
The 1st abdominal spiracles open into the ventral air space, which is enclosed by the pupal mouthparts, wings and legs and which functions in pupal buoyancy.
The processes that rid the adult mosquito body of unwanted substances and ensure homeostasis of the hemolymph under conditions of water and salt loading.
The secretion and regulation of inorganic ions in larvae.

synonyms: vector metabolism resulting in cell growth| vector metabolic process resulting in cell growth| vector metabolism
definition: All the chemical changes which the constituents of the vector undergo. These changes serve two purposes, growth on the one hand and the performance of the work on the other.
The rate at which processes of oxidation take place in the living body, varies within wide limits.
The hormonal involvement in the regulation of enzyme synthesis.

Energy metabolism starts when an insect ingests food, which supplies the fuel from which the chemical energy is liberated. Energy can be gained from lipids, carbohydrates, or proteins, but each one of these compounds cannot be used under every condition. The primary energy stores in insects are the fat body and the haemolymph.

Primarily a mechanism of growth, conditioned by the properties of the cuticle. There are two aspects to the problem of moulting; i) the initiation of the process of the growth and cuticle ii) the determination of those changes in form that occur during ecdysis. Moulting involves all parts of the body, whether supplied with nerves or not, at the same time. Each moult can be considered as a sequence of events.

Little is known of the structure of mosquito larval cuticle other than that the abdomen it consists of a two-layered corrugated epicuticle, a then exocuticle and an endocuticle of some five lamellae. Pore canals are present.

Three hours after larval-pupal ecdysis the epicuticle darkens. The outer seven lamellae of the procuticle which constitute the outer region of exocuticle darken shortly thereafter, and subsequently the epicuticle and outer exocuticle look like a single homogeneous layer. The colour of the pupal abdomen changes from white at ecdysis to grey after one hour and to dark brown after three hours.

Formation of pharate cuticle starts during the later stages of dissolution of the pupal cuticle. Seventeen hours after larval-pupal ecdysis small 3-layered plates are deposited just above the apical membrane of the epidermal cells, which bears minute microvilli at this stage. Addition of material at the edges of the plate leads to the formation of a continuous layer of outer epicuticle over the epidermal cells. By the pupal-adult ecdysis there are four lamellae.
Fifteen hours after larval-pupal ecdysis, apolysis starts. The epidermis separates from the pupal cuticle forming an apolysial space in which a small amount of apolysial fluid accumulates.

The hormone from the neurosecretory cells of the brain activates the thoracic glands and causes them to secrete the moulting hormone. The thoracic glands requie the continued presence of the brain hormone until the "critical period", when mitosis has begun and there is an adequate supply of moulting hormone in the blood.

During moulting, even when unaccompanied by any striking change of form, there is much reconstruction in the epidermis. New cell divisions and the death and disolution of unwanted nuclei take place simultaneously.
A condition in which growth or development is suspended and physiological activity is diminished.

During the first or second day after emergence, a mosquito undergoes behavioural maturation when, due to the action of hormones and other substances that act on the nervous system, it becomes competent in sexual behaviour.

Male mosquitos become sexually responsive to flying conspecific females 12-36h after emergence, by which time their terminalia have inverted and their antennal fibrilae have become either permanenrly erect or capable of temporary erection.

Observations of the coupling of force-mated or tethered females suggested that refractoriness is expressed through altered responses of the female terminalia to genital contact. Even if coupling occurs, it does not result in sperm transfer.
Is a form of foraging, and it includes responses to the environment at three hierarchical levels: the habitat, the patch or biotope, and the resource item.

The pupae of almost all holometabolous insects are incapable of locomotion; instead the mosquito pupae swim and dive exceptionaly. Although they can swim strongly, they spend most of their time immobile at the water surface.

Mosquito larvae have the usual internal organs of ion regulation and also they have four external balloon-like anal papillae, which are capable of ion uptake from very dilute solution. They are anatomically adapted for the specific characteristics of the water surface, notably the surface forces in the air-water interface. Mosquitoes (mostly Culidis) form part of the neuston-the assemblage of small to medium-sized organisms that live at the water surface.

The movements of the larvae that are oriented directly towards or directly away from stimuli. Prefixes denote the nature of the stimulus. A taxis is positive if directed towards the source, and negative if directed away from it.
Unoriented movements made in response to particular stimuli. The strength of the response is related to intensity of stimulation. Kineses can have prefixes that denote the nature of the stimulus.

The characteristic food resource of mosquito larvae is 'particular matter'. This includes aquatic microorganisms, such as bacteria, diatoms and algae, and also, as an important component, particles of detritus that are largely derived from decayed plant tissues.

Larvae groom themselves by working their mouthparts over accessible parts of the body surface. After their use in feeding and grooming, the mouthparts themselves need to be cleaned, and structures that serve that function are present at the posterior end of the abdomen of the most larvae.

Adult mosquitos have two accurate and sensitive compound eyes. They have the capacity to resolve details of the spatial environment and so permit complex activities such as upwind flight and position holding in swarms. The compound eyes of the adult mosquito arise during the first larval instar as thickenings of the epidermis, called optic placodes, just anterior to the stemmata. Simple structures which differ from the ocelli or single-lens eyes present in the adults of most orders and in the larvae of most non-holometabolous orders of insects.
Both sexes require plant juices as an energy source. Female mosquitoes imbibe blood to obtain protein for ovary development.
The uptake of food ranging from small particles to live invertebrates.

A mode of feeding by females, in which the fascicle is deployed beyond the labella to penetrate the skin of the host, and a large volume of blood is imbibed and passed into the midgut. Blood feeding can be divided into four phases.
Is the removal of particles suspended in the water column or associated with the water surface.
Is the removal and ingestion of the biofilm that abheres tightly to submerged plant and mineral surfaces, and also of the algae and stalked protists that adhere directly to such surfaces.
The gnawing and biting-off of small fragments of tissue, whether from plantsor dead invertebrates.
Is the resuspension and removal of particles deposited on or loosely attached to surfaces.
Some mosquito larvae seize and engulf other insects, and often of their own size. The prey is swallowed whole.
Mosquito larvae imbibe substantial volumes of water when feeding and also drink extensively in the absence of food.
Declining flow rate of urine production.
Very rapid flow in the first minutes after the blood meal.
When the flow rate is slightly above the control level.
Mosquito larvae pass through four instars. Growth is continuous throughout each instar, as can be seen in the progressive increase in size of the body regions that are covered with thin cuticle.
Mosquito larvae pass through four instar. Each instar is a stage of development but also growth.
The retraction of the epidermis from the cuticle.
The final stage of moulting. Shedding of what remains of the old cuticle.
The ecdysis between any of the four larval instars.
The ecdysis between the larval and the pupal stage.
The emergence of the adult mosquito from the pupal cuticle.

The rudiments of some imaginal disks are present in newly hatched larvae and develop slowly during the larval stage; others appear as late as the 3rd instar. Each imaginal disk is first apparent as a plate of columnar epidermal cells which grows slowly with cell division. Increase in size of the imaginal disks occurs principally during the 4th instar, accompanied by numerous mitoses, and in most cases the disks are shaped only very approximately like the adult appendages at the time.
The development and differentiation of the gonads and primary sexual characters.

concept_name: development of the central nervous system

In those invertebrates with a central nervous system it typically consists of a brain, cerebral ganglia and a nerve cord.
name_normalized: development of the central nervous system

definition: The development of the compound eyes proceeds in a sequence of events - first determination and cellular proliferation, then differentiation - which pass as waves across a region of the head epidermis, the 'prospective eye field', that will transform into the compound eye.

At metamorphosis some of the tissues that have endopolyploid nuclei undergo somatic reduction and cell divistion to yield a large number of small, apparently de-differentiated cells which are competent to form adult tissues.

concept_name: response of single-walled multiporous hair sensilla
synonyms: responses of trichoid sensilla|responses of A1 sensilla|responses of A2 sensilla
definition: They are sensitive to olfactory stimuli and occur abundantly on the antennal flagella. The hairs are pointed or blunt and arise without sockets.
name_normalized: response of single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

concept_name: responses of short blunt single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

name_normalized: responses of short blunt single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

concept_name: responses of short pointed single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

name_normalized: responses of short pointed single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

name_normalized: responses of long pointed single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

Also the pattern of information provided by these cells could be intergrated to allow refined discrimination of fatty acid odours.
name_normalized: responses of blunt single-walled multiporous hair sensilla

concept_name: response of single-walled multiporous peg sensilla

definition: The pegs, which arise from shallow depressions in the integument, are usually club-shaped but sometimes finger shaped. They are sensitive to olfactory stimuli.
name_normalized: response of single-walled multiporous peg sensilla

definition: Electrophysiological studies with extracellular electrodes (on female Aedes aegypti) showed that the neurone producing the largest action potentials was the only one sensitive to carbon dioxide. The neuron with the smallest spike height is sensitive to octenol. This neurone produces bursts of action potentials upon exposure of a sensillum to 2 s pulses of CO2-free air that had passed through a stimulus cartidge containing solutions of 1-octen-3-ol in mineral oil. The sensitivity of the mosquito neurones to 1-octen-3-ol was said to be equivalent to that of lepidopteran sensory neurones to pheromones when tested by similar protocols for stimulus preparation and delivery.

concept_name: response of double-walled multiporous peg sensilla
synonyms: responses of A3 sensilla|responses of sensilla basiconica|responses of grooved legs
definition: The grooved peg sensilla of Aedes aegypti contain from two to five neurones, usually three. Spike analysis of extracellular recordings from grooved peg sensilla of Aedes epactius revealed spontaneous action potentials of three distinct amplitudes.
name_normalized: response of double-walled multiporous peg sensilla

definition: When exposed to lactic acid vapour, the grooved peg sensilla of Aedes aegypti exhibited one of three firing patterns: (i) a phasic-tonic increase in spike frequency; (ii) a tonic decrease in the frequency of spontaneous spikes; or (iii) no change in spike frequency. Thus neurones are excited or inhibited or are non-responsive.

Electrophysiological evidence from different insects suggests that hygrosensory neurons occur in poreless sensilla. It is thought that absorption of water vapour by the cuticular wall results in deformation of the sensillum.

The reception of the physical stimuli is typically a three-stage process of coupling, transduction and encoding. Is made by the mosquito antennae, which are sensitive to a band of vibrational frequencies, pressure changes or displacements of air particles.
Mechanical deformation of the dendritic membrane, producing receptor potentials.
Is the conversion of receptor potentials to action potentials, which are beleived to arise in the cell membrane of the sensory neurone close to the junction between the cell body and axon.

concept_name: responses of the visual pigments and the chromophores
definition: Conjugated proteins which are integral constituents of the membranes of photoreceptor organelles. Each consists of a chromophore and a apoprotein to which it is covalently linked. A number of different visual pigments are known from insect eyes.
name_normalized: responses of the visual pigments and the chromophores

definition: When the chromophore is in the 11-cis configuration, the principal absorption peak of different visual pigments may appear anywhere in the spectrum between ultraviolet and yellow.

When the chromophore is in the all-trans configuration, and the visual pigment is in the meta-state,the absorption peak appears within a much narrower range, usually in the blue but in higher Diptera in the orange.

The spectral sensitivity of a photoreceptor is determined by the absorption characteristics of its visual pigments. The eyes of different insects contain from one to four receptor types with distinct spectral sensitivities. Mosquito larvae exhibit a negative phototactic or diving response when first exposed to light at night or to a bright source by day, but this is soon followed by a return to the surface.
A compound eye with no separation between the crystalline-cone layer and the retinula, each rhabdom receiving light only from its own corneal lens.
A compound eye in which a clear space is interposed between the dioptric apparatus and the retinula, and light from several corneal lenses falls on each rhabdom, producing a much brighter image.
A compound eye in certain diptera in which the rhabdomeres act as independent light guides.

For an eye to be capable of resolving fine detail, the angular separation between the receptors must be small. Therefore, in compound eyes the smaller the angle between the optical axes of two adjacent ommatidia, the greater the potential of the eye to resolve detail. The interommatidial angle can be measured in a number of ways.
The sensitivity (S) of an eye is a measure of the size of the photon sample that it can capture from each direction.

concept_name: minimum resolvable angle of an eye
definition: For an eye for a grating (not for a point) is twice the interommatidial angle.
name_normalized: minimum resolvable angle of an eye

definition: Is the highest spatial frequency that an eye can resolve.
The angular sensitivity of an ommatidium is determined by three parameters: (i) optical blurring by the lens; (ii) the width of the rhabdom tip; nad (iii) the waveguide properties of the rhabdom.
The half-width of the Airy disc and the half-width of the rhabdom acceptance function combine to give the half-width of the ommatidial acceptance angle.

The rhabdoms of most insects are cylindrical in form and act as light guides, i.e. they trap and retain light by total internal reflection. The cone of light that such a cylinder can trap is narrow. The acceptance angle of the cylinder is limited by the critical angle for total internal reflection, and therefore is governed by the differenece of refractive index between the receptor itself and the surrounding cytoplasm.

In some bodies of water, but not all, the water surface is a hazardous place due to predators. Larvae gain protection by a variety of means, including the occupation of transient biotopes, which often lack predators, or avoidance responses given to surface vibration or visual stimuli.
They are an important part of feeding behaviour, causing larvae to remain in the location of food sources.
When the turning increases with stimulus strength.
When the turning decreases with stimulus strength.
When the movement increases with stimulus strength.

Secretion occurs in two phases and results in formation of the two layers of the chorion, the endochorion and exochorion. Use of the terms 'vitelline membrane' or 'vitelline envelope' for the endochorion is inappropriate.

concept_name: hardening and darkening of the chorion
definition: At oviposition the eggs are soft and white but within an hour the chorion begins to darken and harden. Colour development is uniform over the entire surface of the egg, and after 4h the egg shell looks black and is relatively firm. Superficially at least this process resembles sclerotization.
name_normalized: hardening and darkening of the chorion

definition: Flying in the absense of resource cues.

concept_name: activation while settled on a support
definition: Mosquitoes can be activated by host cues at any time. Unfed, resting females of some species will attack at any hour if disturbed in their shelters by intrusion of a host or stimulated by odour from a nearby host. Such opportunistic biting has been observed in nocturnal mosquitoes disturbed by day. The activation step is readily observed in the laboratory but has seldom been described from the field.
name_normalized: activation while settled on a support

definition: If the stimulus is sight of a moving host, the activated mosquito, may fly directly to the host.
If the stimulus is olfactory but there is no air movement, as can happen in the laboratory the response is kinetic, i.e an increase in flight speed or frequency of turning.

Known kairomones include carbon dioxide, octenol, lactic acid and water vapour. Carbon dioxide activates mosquitoes and is used in odour-mediated anemotaxis. Octenol and lactic acid act additively and possibly in some instances synergistically with carbon dioxide.
The follicle has increased in size considerably but without changing shape. The oocyte occupies >50% to 70% of the length of the follicle.

The follicle has grown further and has become slightly narrower, starting to assume the shape of a mature oocyte. The oocyte occupies 90% of the follicle length. The nurse cells still appear intact and occupy about 10% of the follicle length.

The follicle assumes the shape of the mature oocyte, or almost so, but has not reached full length. The nurse cells have degenerated and at first stain bright crimson with neutral red; later in this stage they disappear. Chorionic structures start to appear.

The oocyte structures its full length. The follicular epithelium degenerates. Chorionic structures such as the floats (Anopheles), micropyle cup (Culex) or surface sculpturing (Aedes) become fully formed.
Attractants are substances that induces gravid females to make oriented movements towards its source.

The juvenile hormone in females of Aedes aegypti increases markedly between 24 and 72h after emergence. Circumstancial evidence associating JH with onset of responsiveness to host cues was obtained with diapausing mosquitoes. Application of large doses of the JH analogue methoprene to diapausing females of Anopheles freeborni and Culex tarsalis hastened their diapause development, including responsiveness to vertebrate hosts.

Juvenile hormones is released after eclosion and stimulates the devlopment of host-seeking behaviour. Little is known about the regulation of juvenile hormone secretion in mosquitoes. Decapitation immediately after emergence has the same effect on follicle development as allatectomy, which suggests that the brain is involved.

concept_name: regulation of follicle growth and competenece
definition: Two developmental gates control the course of previtellogenic development.
name_normalized: regulation of follicle growth and competenece

definition: When present, the deterrents (non-volatile substances) inhibit oviposition .

The weight of evidence suggests that gravid females respond negatively to chemical substances emanating from certain predators, but proof of this requires that these substances be isolated, identified and tested as repellents or deterents.
Gravid females make oriented movements away from its source of any oviposition repellent.
Electophysiological analysis of the reflex response showed that the labellar muscles are activated some 40ms after stimulation of the aboral sensilla with sucrose.

concept_name: adult response of olfactory sensilla while feeding on plant sugar

name_normalized: adult response of olfactory sensilla while feeding on plant sugar

concept_name: adult response of olfactory sensilla while host-seeking

name_normalized: adult response of olfactory sensilla while host-seeking

definition: Host odour is here taken to comprise all volatile compounds, organic and inorganic, that emanate from a vertebrate host and that stimulate mosquito chemosensilla.
Short, single walled, multiporous hair sensilla on the antennae of females Aedes, Culex and Anopheles give electrical responses to volatile compounds suspected of being oviposition-site attractants.

Fatty acids, i.e. saturated and unsaturated monobasic carboxylic acids, when active with gravid females, tended to induce negative responses. Saturated fatty acids from C2 to C11 yielded significant negative responses.
Mosquitoes that belong to this category contain three types of neurones that variously are excited by lactic acid vapour, inhibited by it or unresponsive to it.

concept_name: response to chemical cue during pre-oviposition stage and oviposition
definition: Behavioural responses of the female to chemical stimuli during the stages of pre-oviposition and oviposition.
name_normalized: response to chemical cue during pre-oviposition stage and oviposition

definition: In nature mosquitoes feed on nectar or blood. Like some other blood-sucking Diptera, usually pass nectar and other plant juices to the crop and dorsal diverticula, but pass blood to the stomach. This separation of nectar and blood permits females to store nectar meal in the crop, passing slowly to the midgut for absorption, while leaving the stomach empty to receive a blood meal at any time.
Stimulants are substances that elicit oviposition.
The responses of mosquitoes to artificial objects have important implications for trap design, but their biological significance is uncertain.
Shade can affect mosquito responses.
Behavioural patterns expressed as a reaction to visual stimuli.

Larvae and pupae that are at the water surface respond to certain stimuli with escape behaviour, often called an alarm response. Usually this takes the form of diving, and at a visibly more rapid rate than in descents made for feeding.
It is reported that mosquitoes - whether diurnal, crepuscular or nocturnal in activity - fed most often from lighter flowers.

When the tarsi of a walking mosquito touch a drop of sugar solution the mosquito stops moving or turns, and directs its proboscis towards the stimulus. The tip of the proboskis is placed in contact with the fluid, and when the chemosensory hairs on the aboral surface of the labella are stimulated the labellar lobes spread apart giving the so-called labellar response. Once the labellar lobes have parted, the oral surfaces of the ladella lie flat on the droplet and the external surfaces face away
The act of depositing eggs.
Mosquitoes conform with other insects in maintaining lipid and glycogen stores in the fat body. Glycogen is also stored in the flight muscles, and trehalose is stored in the haemolymph.
Anoplines exhibit a variety of oviposition behaviours. None oviposited though while settled on the water surface. A number of anopelines will deposit eggs on moist surfaces.

After a period of flying to and against the roof of the cage, the mosquitoes began to make descents to the floor. Often this was an ordinary diagonal flight movement, but sometimes this descent was a 'pancake landing'.

A female that had touched the water surface changed her mode of flight abruptly, beginning to hover, with little displacement in space. Sometimes she stayed in almost exactly the same spot or bobbed up and down 10mm or so vertically or obliqely, or she might swing through an arc of 20-100mm dipping at each end.

Once arrived at the floor, the mosquitoes flew about at speeds 0,36m/s and at height that usually was 20-40mm. In the course of this horizontal flight they dipped again and again to touch the floor, at spaced intervals varying between 0,06-0,2m. The direction appeared to be random.

concept_name: response to optical cue during pre-oviposition stage and oviposition

name_normalized: response to other visual and physical parameters during pre-oviposition stage and oviposition

definition: Chromaticity results from (i)its hue, or dominant wavelengths, and (ii) its chroma (saturation), the extend to which the predominant colour is unadulterated with white. concept_name: response to lightness of the water surface

name_normalized: response to lightness of the water surface

The extent of the carbohydrate and lipid reserves and of the protein content of mosquitoes.

This height varies from very moderate to very substantial, the most elevated larval habitats being those of some forest-inhabiting species that live in tree-holes or epiphytic bromeliads.

concept_name: response to certain combination of factors
definition: The responses of gravid females to particular oviposition-site characteristics might change when experienced simultaneously with other characteristics.
name_normalized: response to certain combination of factors

definition: The species Anopheles minimus is known to lay eggs in small, shaded pools adjacent to running water. The females were little influenced by continuous surface ripples.
For its acceptability to gravid females, three characteristics of soil are important, namely: the soil type, the moisture content and the soil texture.
Conversion of the digestion products into glycogen and triacylglycerol deposits.
Meals of sugar lead to the deposition of glycogen and lipid in the fat body and of glycogen in the flight muscles.
The mechanisms through which sexual behaviour is regulated.

Teneral females are unable to responde to host cues or take a blood meal, but during the first days after emergence their mouthparts and other organs become functional and they develop behavioural capabilities.

The extent of the reserves depends upon the quality of larval nutrition, and there is some variability betweeen species in the proportions of glycogen and lipid. Unlike the higher Diptera, mosquito adults do not develop and 'adult fat body' differing in struct
In behavioural terms, aggregation is a congregation of animals that does not depend upon social attraction. Such behaviours are due to the fact that most habitats are not uniform.
The attack and consumption of conspecific larvae of the same or an earlier instar.
The presence of a predator has a damping effect on larvae movement. But at higher predator densities larval movement increased again slightly, possibly due to disturbance by the predators.
The larvae and pupae of some culicuds are able to lighten or darken their body colour in accordance with the lightness or darkness of the background; others lack this ability.
This is an important form of predator avoidance. A variety of relatively safe niches can be discerned among ground waters.
The "grooming" of other individuals has been considered a form of aggresive behaviour and an aspect of feeding.
While in depth, a larva remains motionless, often when near or underneath a leaf.
Behavioural patterns of gravid females that result in arrival at potential oviposition sites and indicate the suitability of such sites are termed pre-oviposition behaviour.
During growth the larval stage the alimentary canal grows in cell size and with the formation of polytene and endopolyploid nuclei.
The antennal centres grow slowly compared to the brain as a whole during the larval stage (k=0,8) and very rapidly about the time of larval-pupal ecdysis (k=4).

definition: The central body grows most actively in the 4th instar (k=2).

The phenol oxidase enzymes are thought to be central to melanin formation. During encapsulation, polyphenol derivates probably cross-link with proteins from the haemolymph and haemocytes.

In most arthropodes encapsulation is initiated when granular haemocytes degranulate upon contact with foreign bodies, and release components of a phenoloxidase-activating system which adhere to them. Plasmatocytes then enclose the foreign objects within an envelope of hihgly flattened cells which becomes pigmented.

Ovulation is defined as the extrusion of mature oocytes from the ovarian follicles into the calyces and oviducts. Ovulated oocytes enter the vagina, from which they are extruded through the gonotreme at oviposition. Sperm penetrate an oocyte while it is within the vagina. Very soon after oviposition the oocyte chromosomes complete meiosis, and at that stage the oocyte is considered to have transformed into an egg.

Great changes take place in the muscular system during metamorphosis. Most larval head muscles are histolysed but some are carried over to the adult, developing the fine structure of adult muscle and aquiring new relationships with different parts of the head. New muscles arise and the sides and floor of the head become traversed by belts of small myoblasts whose origin is uncertain.

concept_name: metamorphosis of the muscles of the thorax and abdomen
definition: The muscles of the thorax and abdomen are carried over to the adult but the main part of the adult thoracic musculature is new, including the muscles of the appendages, largely formed within the imaginal buds, and the indirect flight muscles. The larval abdominal muscles degenerate early in adult life, having been used for swimming by the pupa and pharate adult. Movements of the adult abdomen are due to small adult muscles which develop from myoblasts in the pupa. Histolysis of the musculature,
name_normalized: metamorphosis of the muscles of the thorax and abdomen

definition: Sexual dimorphism in adult mosquitoes is expressed in a number of ways: (i) in the structure of the gonads; (ii) in th eprimary sexual characters which are derived from the genital imaginal disks; and (iii) in secondary sexual characters such as the adult antennae, maxillary palps and body size. Innate behavioural differences between the sexes reflets dimorphism in the structure and function of the nervous system.

concept_name: kinetic response to food and dissolved nutrient
definition: Mosquito larvae accumulate in regions where there is food because they make an orthokinetic response to soluble contituents diffusing from the food.
name_normalized: kinetic response to food and dissolved nutrient

If exposed to bright light, fourth instar larvae moved about incessantly at the water surface and dived frequently. When by chance they entered a shaded part of the container they became inactive; as a result, almost all larvae congregated in the shade.

Arrestant is substance that induces animals to remain in its presense through their undirected kinetic responses, either by stopping their locomotion (orthokinesis), or changing their rate of turning (klinokinesis).
Attractan is substance that induces animals to make oriented movements towards its source.
A larva spontaneously separates itself from the water surface and descends with a swimming component.
A submerged larva, while feeding, moves anteriorly propelled by currents generated by the actions of its mouthparts.
Tactic responses to chemical compounds.
Tactical responses to gravitation.
Tactic responses to light.
Is described as a tendency to maintain bodily contact with solid objects.

(ii) A vitellogenic stage. (iii) A termination stage.
In newly emerged females the cytoplasm of each trophocyte was rich in reserves, containing lipid droplets, glycogen bodies, and three types of membrane-bounded protein granule.
During this stage, the nucleolus became more multilobed, ribosome proliferation had been renewed, and the rough endoplasmic reticulum was undergoin reorganization.

Termination of vitellogenin synthesis starts with a sharp decline in the concentration of vitellogenin in the fat body. This decline is thought to be associated with a simultaneous and dramatic rise in lysosomal activity.

During the privitellogenic phase of each ovarian cycle the fat body is made competent for vitellogenin synthesis. Stimulated by juvenile hormone, the trophocytes bacame polyploid and their nucleoli enlarge.

The mechanism regulating termination of vitellogenin synthesis remains to be fully elucidated. Lysosomal degradation causes the termination but whether this is programmed solely by the fat body or whether other factors are involved remain uncertain.

When kept with prey in small containers, Toxorhynchites fourth instar larvae that have reached an advanced stage of development stop feeding but continue killing.

definition: The sugars in plant fluids are an extensively used energy source for both males and females. Mosquitoes also obtain plant-derived sugars from other insects and their excretions. Plant fluids provide both sugars and water, and are an important component of mosquito nutrition.

Acquiring plant sugars from other insects.
